sourceArticle.title: OpusClip: #1 AI video clipping tool to create viral shorts
sourceArticle.author: Unknown

athenaOutput.directive: Establish a sovereign, automated video repurposing pipeline through component orchestration. We will bypass closed-SaaS dependencies by integrating existing open-weight models (Whisper, local LLMs, OpenCV/FFmpeg) into a unified Creative Liberation Engine DAG, achieving OpusClip-level capabilities on owned infrastructure.
athenaOutput.rationale: Article I (Sovereignty) demands we own our infrastructure, while Article XXV (Integration Over Reverse-Engineering) explicitly forbids reverse-engineering existing tools. Instead of cloning OpusClip's proprietary code, we will download and orchestrate best-in-class open-source components. By treating LLMs merely as reasoning components (Article XXIII) to identify viral hooks from Whisper transcripts, and using FFmpeg for the mechanical extraction, we create a superior, sovereign content multiplier pipeline.

options.title: The Sovereign OSS Pipeline (Whisper + LLM + FFmpeg)
options.description: Download and utilize existing open-source models natively on the NAS. Use Whisper for timestamped transcription, a local LLM to analyze the transcript for high-engagement 'hooks', and OpenCV/FFmpeg to handle face-tracking, cropping, and subtitle rendering.
options.tradeoffs: Maximum sovereignty and zero recurring costs. High initial setup complexity for the pipeline orchestration. Requires robust GPU resources on the NAS for timely processing.

options.title: OpusClip API Sovereign Bridge
options.description: If OpusClip offers an API, build a secure, isolated adapter (via SIGNAL) to use it as a stateless processing node. Send video, receive clips, and immediately purge external data.
options.tradeoffs: Fastest time-to-market and leverages proven external algorithms. Violates strict biometric/data sovereignty if sensitive internal videos are processed. Creates vendor lock-in and recurring API costs.

options.title: Hybrid Edge-Cloud Orchestration
options.description: Perform secure transcript generation and 'viral moment' identification locally on the NAS (Edge). Only dispatch the specific 30-second raw clips to an external cloud rendering engine for advanced visual polish, captions, and B-roll insertion.
options.tradeoffs: Balances local data security (full videos never leave the NAS) with advanced cloud rendering capabilities. Still relies on external vendors for the final visual asset.

options.title: Real-Time SHOWRUNNER Broadcast Clipping
options.description: Integrate clipping mechanics directly into the ATLAS/SHOWRUNNER Broadcast Hive. Instead of post-processing long-form VODs, maintain a rolling 60-second buffer during live streams and use an LLM to trigger instant 'clip' commands based on live audio analysis.
options.tradeoffs: Creates instant viral assets during live events. Highly complex memory management and requires ultra-low latency LLM inference. Not applicable for existing backlog of VODs.

options.title: Omni-Channel Asset Multiplier DAG
options.description: Expand the scope beyond video. Have DIRECTOR orchestrate a DAG that takes one long-form video and simultaneously produces viral shorts (video), podcast snippets (audio), and SEO-optimized blog posts (text) using a single processing pass.
options.tradeoffs: Maximizes the ROI of the processing compute. High architectural complexity requiring coordination across PALETTE (brand), SAGE (text), and GRAPHICS (video).

options.title: Custom Viral-Hook Vision Model Training
options.description: Leveraging the prior strategic realization that foundation models are cheap (~$1,500), train a custom multimodal model from scratch specifically designed to detect visual and auditory 'viral hooks' in our specific content niche.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article XXV (Integration over Reverse-Engineering) by attempting to rebuild a solved problem from scratch. Unnecessary expenditure of compute and time when off-the-shelf LLMs can analyze transcripts effectively.

constitutionalFlags: Article XXIII: LLMs Are Components, Not Architecture
